            echo "  ▸ affiliate → bash ci.sh (affiliate gate)"
            # Feed the buffered push ref lines to ci.sh stdin: ci.sh builds
            # each extension only when the pushed range touches it (2026-10-14
            # narrowing), but stdin is already consumed above, so without this
            # it would see EOF and build both extensions on every push.
            if ! ( cd "$REPO_ROOT/affiliate" && printf '%s' "$PUSH_LINES" | bash ci.sh ) > /tmp/pre-push-affiliate-ci.log 2>&1; then
                GATES_FAILED="$GATES_FAILED

                FAIL=1
            fi
            continue
        fi

        # through a QUOTED heredoc — no shell interpolation inside the node
        # program, so no nested quoting to get wrong.
        #
        # Print one TAB-separated `GATE<TAB>command` line per gate, ALWAYS for
        # all four gates (empty command when the script is absent).
        #
        # Fix 2026-10-14. The old code only emitted a gate when the workspace
        # defined it, then read it back with `eval CMD="$WS_${GATE}"` under
        # `set -u`. A workspace like packages/nightfall — whose package.json
        # defines only `test` — therefore aborted the hook with
        # "WS_TYPECHECK: unbound variable" and failed every push that touched
        # it. Reading the pairs straight into the loop removes both the
        # unbound-variable hazard and the eval entirely.
        GATE_LINES=$(PKG_JSON="$PKG_JSON" node <<'NODE'
    const fs = require("fs");
    const p = process.env.PKG_JSON;
    let s = {};
    if (fs.existsSync(p)) {
        try {

        } catch (e) {
            process.stderr.write("pre-push: unparseable " + p + ": " + e.message + "\n");
        }
    }
    const found = {
        TYPECHECK: s.compile || s.typecheck || s.check || "",
        BUILD: s.build || "",
        TEST: s.test || "",
        LINT: s.lint || "",
    };
    for (const k of ["TYPECHECK", "BUILD", "TEST", "LINT"]) {
        // TAB-separated: gate names and script bodies never contain a TAB,
        // and a script body may legitimately contain spaces and shell
        // metacharacters, which `IFS=... read` preserves intact.
        console.log(k + "\t" + (found[k] || ""));
    }

    )

        # avoids re-expanding `$`/backticks inside a gate command.
        GATE_FILE=$(mktemp /tmp/.pre-push-gates.XXXXXX)
        printf '%s\n' "$GATE_LINES" > "$GATE_FILE"
        while IFS="$TAB" read -r GATE CMD; do
            if [ -z "$CMD" ]; then

            fi
            WS_TAG=$(echo "$WS" | tr '/' '_')

            # workspace. We must look at both.

            # PATH list. Prepending ROOT_BIN here made the hoisted root
            # tsc/wxt shadow the workspace's own .bin, contradicting the
            # comment above (workspace .bin first).
            [ -d "$WS_BIN" ] && EXTRA_BIN="$EXTRA_BIN$WS_BIN:"

                FAIL=1
            fi
            cd "$REPO_ROOT" || exit 1
        done < "$GATE_FILE"

    //! Deterministic userspace faults; all commands are constructor-injected and

    use super::*;
    use std::process::Command;
    
    fn fixture() -> (tempfile::TempDir, IndexBatch) {
        let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        assert!(Command::new("git")
            .args(["init", "-q"])
            .arg(dir.path())
            .status()
            .unwrap()
            .success());
        std::fs::write(dir.path().join("file"), b"staged").unwrap();
        assert!(Command::new("git")
            .current_dir(dir.path())
            .args(["add", "file"])
            .status()
            .unwrap()
            .success());
        let mut batch = IndexBatch::with_cwd(dir.path().to_owned());
        batch.budget = Duration::from_millis(150);
        (dir, batch)
    }
    
    fn failure_then_recovery(script: &str, path: &str, resolver: bool) {
        let (_dir, mut batch) = fixture();
        batch.scripts[usize::from(!resolver)] = Some(script.to_owned());
        let start = Instant::now();
        let indexed = batch.lookup(path, 1024);
        assert_eq!(indexed, None);
        assert!(
            start.elapsed() < Duration::from_secs(2),
            "deadline/cleanup exceeded"
        );
        assert!(batch.live.is_none());
        // Fresh, in-memory test identity: no process-global key initialization.
        let mut security = dracon_security_kit::WardenSecurity::new(None)
        failure_then_recovery("read query; printf 'bad\\n'", "file", false);
        failure_then_recovery("read query; printf 'abc blob 67108865\\n'", "file", false);
        failure_then_recovery("exit 1", "file", false);
    }
    
    #[test]
    fn index_batch_reuses_authenticated_staged_ciphertext() {
        let (dir, mut batch) = fixture();
        let mut security = dracon_security_kit::WardenSecurity::new(None)
            .unwrap()
            .with_managed_patterns(vec!["credentials".into()]);
        security.add_memory_identity(age::x25519::Identity::generate());
        let input = b"isolated synthetic credential";
        let ciphertext = security
            .clean_reusing_index(input, "credentials", None)
            .unwrap();
        std::fs::write(dir.path().join("credentials"), &ciphertext).unwrap();
        assert!(Command::new("git")
            .current_dir(dir.path())
            .args(["add", "credentials"])
            .status()
            .unwrap()
            .success());
        let indexed = batch.lookup("credentials", 1024 * 1024).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(indexed, ciphertext);
        assert_eq!(
            security
                .clean_reusing_index(input, "credentials", Some(&indexed))
                .unwrap(),
            ciphertext
        );
    }

    /// Auto-create the forge-side repos for an existing local repo that
    /// already has remotes configured (added by `configure_standard_remotes_if_missing`)
    /// but the corresponding github/gitlab/codeberg repo may not yet
    /// exist. Does NOT push — that's the job of `push_mirror_remotes`.
    ///
    /// ADDED 2026-07-21 (v0.112.29) for the empty-local-repo case where
    /// `is_repo_ready` returns false (no commits) and `push_mirror_remotes`
    /// would silently skip. Calling `auto_create_all_remotes` standalone
    /// ensures the forge-side repos exist when the operator's first commit
    /// lands. Idempotent: each remote is checked via `git ls-remote`
    /// (`remote_repo_exists`) before any `gh repo create` / `glab repo create`
    /// / REST call. Honored per-remote `auto_create` flag (codeberg
    /// defaults to false since v0.112.28's quota posture).
    /// implementation removed ANY non-`origin` remote not in `keep` —
    /// silently destroying OPERATOR-added remotes (`backup`,
    /// `mirror-to-nas`, forks) on every push cycle. A remote is now
    /// removed only when the daemon manages it: either it carries the
    /// `dracon.managed-<name> = true` config marker (stamped by
    /// `ensure_remote`), or its name is in `managed_names` (the current
    /// policy remote list — covers pre-marker-era remotes like the
    /// codeberg remote the v0.112.30 exclusion removes).
    pub(crate) fn remove_stale_remotes(
        repo: &Path,
        keep: &[&str],
        managed_names: &[&str],
    ) -> Result<()> {
        let current = list_remotes(repo);
        let keep_set: HashSet<_> = keep.iter().collect();
        for remote in current {
            if remote == "origin" {
                continue;
            }
            if keep_set.contains(&remote.as_str()) {
                continue;
            }
            let managed = managed_names.iter().any(|n| *n == remote)
                || std_git_command()
                    .args(["config", "--get", &format!("dracon.managed-{}", remote)])
                    .current_dir(repo)
                    .output()
                    .map(|o| o.status.success() && String::from_utf8_lossy(&o.stdout).trim() == "true")
                    .unwrap_or(false);
            if !managed {
                if debug_enabled() {
                    eprintln!(
                        "🐛 {} keeping operator-added remote {} (not daemon-managed)",
                        repo.display(),
                        remote
                    );
                }
                continue;
            }
            std_git_command()
                .args(["remote", "remove", &remote])
                .current_dir(repo)
                .status()
                .with_context(|| format!("git remote remove {} in {}", remote, repo.display()))?;
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    # AGENTS.md — dracon-platform
    
    > Applies to this repo and every nested game repo under
    > `web/games/<wip|released>/<name>/` (hegemon, deathrun, endless-td,
    > darklord, neonbreak, junk-runner, polis, …).
    
    ## Design principle: desktop-only
    
    All games in this portfolio target **desktop only**. Do not attempt
    dual desktop+mobile support — it dilutes both experiences and leads to
    failure (the market is already saturated with phone games that try to do
    both). Every game entry in `web/games/libs/data/games-catalog.json` carries
    `"target_platform": "desktop"` to enforce this. If a game's build or
    runtime attempts to serve mobile viewport adaptations, flag it as a
    regression.
    
    ### Desktop-only scope: narrow-window robustness is not phone adaptation (DECIDED 2026-09-04)
    
    The desktop-only law bans phone-market adaptation (touch-first layouts,
    mobile viewports, app-store packaging) — it does NOT ban rendering
    correctly in a narrow desktop window. Snapped / split-screen / tiled
    windows under 600 CSS px are normal desktop usage, so per-route
    `@media (max-width: 600px)` blocks, Svelte `matchMedia` resize handlers
    (neonbreak CLAUDE.md rule 6), and the visual-probe 390x844 sweep exist to
    keep the desktop layout legible when the window is narrow — not to serve
    phones. Do not delete narrow-window handling for literal conformance, and
    do not read its presence as permission to add phone adaptation: the
    games-catalog `"target_platform": "desktop"` invariant still governs.
    
    ### Music-app exception: full mobile-web support (DECIDED 2026-09-15)
    
    The desktop-only law stands for every game — but the **music app
    (`web/music`) is exempt**: music must work fully in phone and
    tablet browsers (touch-first layouts, 390px portrait, 768px
    tablet, phone landscape), because funneling listeners toward an
    app they don't have breaks the core loop — they should stay on
    the site. Concretely: `web/music` may ship `pointer: coarse`
    target passes, phone/tablet/landscape layout rules, and an
    emulated-mobile Playwright suite (`tests/music-mobile-35.spec.ts`)
    — none of which count as game regressions. The games-catalog
    `"target_platform": "desktop"` invariant is unchanged (music is
    not a catalog game). Desktop layout must not regress under any
    mobile rule (proven by the desktop E2E neighbors on every pass).
    
    ## dracon-sync daemon: git-history rules for agent loops
    
    This repo is watched by the **dracon-sync daemon**, which auto-commits
    working-tree changes within ~3-10 seconds and pushes them to all
    remotes (github/gitlab/codeberg) immediately after.
    
    **NEVER rewrite history in this repo.** Specifically, never:
    
    - `git commit --amend` — any commit may already be pushed
    - `git rebase`, or `git reset --hard` to an earlier commit
    - `git filter-branch` / `git filter-repo`
    - `git push --force` / `--force-with-lease`
    
    ### SANCTIONED ONE-TIME EXCEPTION (2026-08-13, audit DECIDE git-pack)
    
    User-authorized exception to the no-rewrite rule: a single
    `git filter-repo --invert-paths` pass purging **pi-session HTML
    captures, audit/verification screenshots, and pre-extraction game
    content blobs** (web/games/* media + docs whose history now lives in
    the 10 game submodule repos) from the parent repo's history, to
    shrink the ~477 MiB pack. Authorized procedure ONLY:
    
    1. Document this amendment (commit it BEFORE the purge).
    2. Pause the daemon with the freeze marker: `dracon-sync pause`
       (writes /home/dracon/.dracon/dracon-sync.freeze). NOTE: `systemctl
       --user stop dracon-sync.service` does NOT hold — the unit is
       `Restart=always` and comes straight back; the freeze marker is the
       mechanism the daemon actually respects (observed 2026-08-13/14).
    3. Back up: `git bundle create` the current history (keep the bundle
       OUT of any dracon-sync-watched repo — it gets auto-committed and
       pushed; durable copy e.g. /home/dracon/Backups/).
    4. `git filter-repo --invert-paths --paths-from-file <list>` where the
       list contains ONLY blob paths. Build it from `git ls-tree -r`
       (blob-only) or strip tree entries from `git rev-list --objects
       --all`: bare directory paths in the list make filter-repo delete
       whole subtrees (observed 2026-08-13: 506 dir rules nuked 1,473
       tracked web/games files + the submodule gitlinks; recovered from
       the pre-purge bundle). Never gitlink paths, never code files.
    5. Force-push every remote (`git push --force origin`, `gitlab`;
       gitlab main is branch-protected — unprotect via `glab api`,
       push, re-protect with identical settings).
    6. Resume the daemon: `dracon-sync resume` (or write the freeze
       marker state back).
    
    Execution history under this exception (each pass user-authorized):
    2026-08-13 pass 1 (pi-session/audit-screenshots/web-screenshots/media)
    + pass 2 (user-approved extension: web/games history + cookbook.json);
    2026-08-14 pass 3 (auditor-found residual pi-session capture). The
    "ONE-TIME" clause means: no future rewrite without a new user decision
    and a new amendment — it does not grandfather residual-class paths the
    authorized passes missed. All other no-rewrite rules remain in force.
    
    The daemon's auto-generated commit messages (e.g.
    `2 file(s) in src [...] DELTA:+7/-2`) are **expected and fine**. Do not
    "fix" them by rewriting: a rewritten commit races the already-pushed
    original and creates a divergent branch. The daemon then merges it, the
    next amend drops the merge, and the repo enters a permanent divergence
    loop (observed 2026-07-25 in hegemon — the loop agent's own notes
    documented `filter-branch --msg-filter` + `--force-with-lease` as its
    "recovery" practice — and in browser-extensions-shared via tip amends).
    
    ### What to do instead
    
    - **CHANGED 2026-09-26: do NOT `git commit` (or `git add`) yourself.**
      "First committer wins" racing was retired after 2026-09-25/26, when
      loop-vs-daemon add/commit races left 7 stale `index.lock` files

    # Status inspection lifecycle and retry starvation — 2026-10-15
    
    ## Observed failure
    
    Fleet status showed multiple dirty repositories stalled for hours while PUSH
    still displayed the last successful result. The service was active. Logs showed
    four repositories repeatedly timing out every 60s while others retained
    `status-pending` holds for more than 6,000s. After a restart the same signature
    returned on a different group, including small utility repos.
    
    The earlier increase of the filter-aware classification floor did not fix this
    separate status-inspection lifecycle. Nor does one green fleet snapshot prove
    that either problem cannot recur.
    
    Related incident: parent `docs/design/sync-wedge-filter-hang-2026-10-04.md`.
    
    ## Mechanism and change
    
    The daemon called dracon-git 94.7.2 `GitService::get_status`, which delegates to
    `spawn_blocking`. Aborting its async caller does not cancel the blocking closure
    or its synchronous subprocesses. The scheduler released the reservation but
    could immediately retry the same early repository, creating more blocking work
    and denying later repositories the four global status slots. The specific
    warden-side trigger for a hung filter remains unproven.
    
    `src/git/inspection.rs` replaces only the daemon's status-inspection boundary:
    
    - Git porcelain v2 with branch/ahead/behind and all untracked files;
    - NUL-delimited parsing, including rename source records and non-UTF8 paths;
    - no optional index locks, no hook bypass or filter bypass;
    - existing owned process-group cancellation/capped pipe capture in `git/ops.rs`;
    - bounded runtime: cancellation drops and kills Git plus filter helpers rather
      than merely abandoning an uncancellable blocking job;
    - parse/exit/timeout failures are errors, never fabricated clean snapshots.
    
    `src/daemon.rs` now applies a 300s per-repo retry cooldown on both the watchdog
    abort and an inspection error. Failed early repositories cannot immediately
    reclaim all four slots. The concurrency cap remains four and the status timeout
    remains 60s. No policy, identity, trust list, ownership, history, or bucket
    eligibility setting is changed.
    
    ## Regression evidence
    
    - A real configured clean filter starts a sleeping helper. Inspection times out;
      the helper is confirmed terminated; removing the simulated fault lets a fresh
      inspection succeed.
    - Real unborn repository inspection counts files within an untracked directory.
    - Parser fixtures cover clean/detached/unborn heads, ahead/behind, combined
      changes, rename-source skipping, conflicts, non-UTF8 paths, malformed output.
    - Scheduler regression models four failed early repositories and verifies the
      next four gain admission, with retries admitted exactly at cooldown expiry.
    
    Bounded validation: `timeout 180 cargo test -p dracon-sync --locked status_`,
    `timeout 180 cargo test -p dracon-sync --locked git::inspection`,
    `timeout 590 cargo test --workspace --locked`, and
    `timeout 180 cargo clippy --workspace --locked -- -D warnings` pass.
    `timeout 400 cargo deny check` still fails on existing dependency advisories;
    bans, licenses and sources pass. No advisory exceptions were added.
    
    ## Follow-up: synchronous discovery was still starving result collection
    
    The first deployment did not resolve sustained fleet convergence. A bounded
    `strace` of the daemon coordinator at 14:49 showed `openat`/`getdents64` walking
    `dracon-utilities/target/debug/deps` (19 GiB locally) while its status reservations
    aged. At another observation the service had no live Git children despite status
    holds continuing. The trace proves coordinator-side build-cache enumeration;
    it does not prove the precise cause of every earlier filter timeout.
    
    The global `exclude_dir_names` intentionally omits `target` because using it
    for cleanup/staging had previously damaged vendored source named `target`.
    Restoring that blanket exclusion would regress source safety. Instead:
    
    - Discovery alone recognizes the standard 43-byte `CACHEDIR.TAG` signature and
      prunes those explicitly tagged cache trees. No file is deleted or unstaged;
      untagged source named `target` remains discoverable, as do nested standalone
      utility repos. Explicitly watched roots remain discoverable.
    - `daemon/discovery_scheduler.rs` performs discovery in one background blocking
      job, refreshing at most every 30s. Slow discovery cannot block the coordinator.
      There is never more than one walk in flight, even when a filesystem stalls.
    - Scheduling retains the last complete snapshot for the same watch configuration.
      Initial discovery and configuration changes do not supply partial/old-scope
      snapshots to retain/prune operations. Completed results from an obsolete
      configuration are discarded. Errors retain the last valid snapshot and retry
      after cooldown; a walk exceeding 60s emits a warning without spawning another.
    
    Regression tests cover cache/source distinctions, explicit roots, nested repos,
    blocked discovery retaining a usable snapshot without duplicate walks, and watch
    configuration changes. All 22 discovery tests pass. Full workspace tests,
    Clippy and the release build pass after these changes.
    
    ## Live rollout observations
    
    The discovery build was installed atomically through `dracon-sync maintenance`
    and the service restarted at 15:02 on 2026-10-15. The running executable digest
    matched the tested release. Within two minutes the daemon committed/synced
    .dracon, db-gateway, utilities, neonbreak, deathrun, endless-td and junk-runner,
    and committed the parent platform backlog. The table no longer showed STALLED.
    Browser extensions remained pending with a growing live-generator backlog; that
    is not claimed resolved by the scheduling fix.
    
    The rollout exposed `fatal: unable to create threaded lstat: Resource temporarily
    unavailable` in an ai-auto-writer status. Inspections now use command-local
    `index.threads=1` and `core.preloadIndex=false` so four status inspections do not
    fan out index/preload workers against the shared systemd task limit alongside
    hook runtimes. No persistent Git configuration, filters, hooks, task limit or
    staging policy was weakened.
    
    Final build deployment: 2026-10-15 15:14 BST. Running executable and tested
    release both hash to
    `bcedd8b63a402ba7126020f93148b963be1a92f6eef30057fc119edb26594244`.
    In the observation window through 15:20:47 (more than one 300s retry interval),
    the journal recorded 27 commits and 23 sync completions, no status-inspection
    failure/timeouts, and no discovery-duration warnings. The final table showed
    no STALLED/STUCK rows; browser-extensions-shared was the sole pending push
    (17 ahead with 123 modified and 298 untracked files from ongoing generation).
    There was one platform classification exit-128 failure during this window;
    it retried, and platform was no longer pending at the final snapshot. That
    transient classification failure is not claimed eliminated by this fix.
    
    Final workspace tests: 2,389 passed, zero failures across 35 suites. Clippy and
    release build passed. Dependency advisories remain as recorded above.
    
    Longer-term convergence and browser gate throughput remain to be observed;
    this bounded live result does not claim every fleet gate will always pass.

    //! Repository status checks — origin, upstream, conflict state, readiness.
    
    use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
    
    use anyhow::{Context, Result};
    
    use super::current_branch;
    
    /// RAII guard that acquires `.git/index.lock` using the same protocol git uses.
    ///
    /// Git commands (checkout, add, reset, etc.) hold this lock while modifying
    /// the working tree. By acquiring it too, we guarantee mutual exclusion with
    /// any in-flight git operation. If the lock is held, we skip; if we hold it,
    /// git's checkout waits for us.
    ///
    /// This is the definitive fix for the clone race: during `git clone`, checkout
    /// holds index.lock. Our `ensure_standard_files` / `publish_repo_pubkey`
    /// write files to the working tree. Without the lock, these appear before
    /// checkout completes → "Untracked working tree file would be overwritten by
    /// merge." With the lock, either git holds it (we skip) or we hold it
    /// (git's checkout waits until we're done).
    pub(crate) struct IndexLock {
        path: PathBuf,
        /// True if we successfully created the lock (our responsibility to clean up).
        held: bool,
    }
    
    /// Return the index-lock path Git uses for a checkout.
    ///
    /// A normal checkout stores the lock below `<repo>/.git`, while a linked
    /// worktree or nested submodule exposes `.git` as a pointer file. Resolving
    /// the pointer here keeps startup cleanup and `IndexLock` on the same path
    /// instead of letting one caller inspect a non-existent `<repo>/.git/index.lock`.
    pub(crate) fn index_lock_path(repo: &Path) -> PathBuf {
        crate::git::path_gitdir(repo)
            .map(|gitdir| gitdir.join("index.lock"))
            .unwrap_or_else(|| repo.join(".git").join("index.lock"))
    }
    
    impl IndexLock {
        /// Try to acquire `.git/index.lock` for a repo.
        /// Returns Ok(lock) if acquired, Err if another process holds it.
        /// Uses `O_EXCL` (create_new) for atomic creation — no TOCTOU race.
        pub(crate) fn acquire(repo: &Path) -> Result<Self, String> {
            // CHANGED 2026-07-21 (v0.112.33, audit M16/F2.7): resolve
            // the REAL gitdir first — for linked worktrees and nested
            // submodules (the canonical architecture since 2026-07-02),
            // `<repo>/.git` is a FILE, so creating
            // `<repo>/.git/index.lock` failed with ENOTDIR and
            // `ensure_standard_files` was silently skipped EVERY cycle
            // for every submodule (with a misleading "lock contention"
            // debug message). For a submodule the lock belongs at
            // `<parent>/.git/modules/<name>/index.lock` — where git
            // itself takes it.
            let path = index_lock_path(repo);
            match std::fs::OpenOptions::new()
                .write(true)
                .create_new(true) // O_EXCL — fails if file exists
                .open(&path)
            {
                Ok(_file) => Ok(Self { path, held: true }),
                Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::AlreadyExists => Err(format!(
                    "index.lock held by another git operation, skipping {}",
                    repo.display()
                )),
                Err(e) => Err(format!(
                    "failed to create index.lock for {}: {}",
                    repo.display(),
                    e
                )),
            }
        }
    }
    
    impl Drop for IndexLock {
        fn drop(&mut self) {
            if self.held {
                let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&self.path);
            }
        }
    }
    
    /// Check whether an `origin` remote exists via config or git CLI.
    pub(crate) fn has_origin_remote(repo: &Path) -> bool {
        let config_path = repo.join(".git").join("config");
        if let Ok(config) = std::fs::read_to_string(&config_path) {
            if config
                .lines()
                .any(|line| line.trim() == "[remote \"origin\"]")
            {
                return true;
            }
            // FIXED 2026-10-03 (audit R4-SC-12): a config-parse miss is NOT
            // a verdict — trailing comments, casing, and include-based
            // remotes all read as absent. Fall through to the git CLI,
            // which resolves them natively, instead of returning false.
        }
        crate::policy::std_git_command()
            .arg("remote")
            .arg("get-url")
            .arg("origin")
            .current_dir(repo)
            .output()
            .map(|o| o.status.success())
            .unwrap_or(false)
    }
    
    /// Check whether the current branch has a configured upstream.
    pub(crate) fn has_tracking_upstream(repo: &Path) -> bool {
        let config_path = repo.join(".git").join("config");
        if let Ok(config) = std::fs::read_to_string(&config_path) {
            if let Some(branch) = current_branch(repo) {
                let section = format!("[branch \"{}\"]", branch);
                if let Some(pos) = config.find(&section) {
                    let after = &config[pos + section.len()..];
                    let next_section = after.find('[').unwrap_or(after.len());
                    let branch_config = &after[..next_section];
                    return branch_config.contains("remote = ") && branch_config.contains("merge = ");
                }
            }
            return false;
        }
        // Config file not readable (worktree, symlink, etc.) —
        // fall back to git subprocess which handles these cases natively.
        crate::policy::std_git_command()
            .args(["rev-parse", "--abbrev-ref", "--symbolic-full-name", "@{u}"])
            .current_dir(repo)
            .output()
            .map(|o| o.status.success())
            .unwrap_or(false)
    }
    
    // CHANGED 2026-07-26 (v0.113.2, audit SYNC-H8): resolve the REAL

    fn state_path_exists(repo: &Path, name: &str) -> bool {
        crate::git::path_gitdir(repo)
            .map(|gitdir| gitdir.join(name))
            .unwrap_or_else(|| repo.join(".git").join(name))
            .exists()
    }
    
    /// Whether a rebase operation is in progress.
    pub(crate) fn is_rebase_in_progress(repo: &Path) -> bool {
        state_path_exists(repo, "rebase-merge") || state_path_exists(repo, "rebase-apply")
    }
    
    /// Whether a merge operation is in progress.
    pub(crate) fn is_merge_in_progress(repo: &Path) -> bool {
        state_path_exists(repo, "MERGE_HEAD")
    }
    
    /// Whether a cherry-pick operation is in progress.
    pub(crate) fn is_cherry_pick_in_progress(repo: &Path) -> bool {
        state_path_exists(repo, "CHERRY_PICK_HEAD")
    }
    
    /// Whether a revert operation is in progress (R4-SC-11).
    pub(crate) fn is_revert_in_progress(repo: &Path) -> bool {
        state_path_exists(repo, "REVERT_HEAD")
    }
    
    /// Whether a bisect session is active (R4-SC-11).
    pub(crate) fn is_bisect_in_progress(repo: &Path) -> bool {
        state_path_exists(repo, "BISECT_LOG")
    }

                // staging status for the caller.
                _ => {
                    let _ = iter.next();
                }
            }
        }
        entries
    }
    
    /// Get name-status entries via `git diff --name-status` with custom args.
    pub(crate) async fn git_name_status_entries(
        repo: &Path,
        args: &[&str],
    ) -> Result<Vec<(PathBuf, FileStatus)>> {
        // CHANGED 2026-07-21 (v0.112.33, audit M17/F2.8): `-z` (raw,
        // NUL-delimited paths — non-ASCII filenames no longer dropped)
        // and non-zero exits now propagate as Err instead of reading as
        // "zero changed files".
        let output = crate::git::tokio_git_cmd()
            .args(args)
            .arg("-z")
            .current_dir(repo)
            .stdout(std::process::Stdio::piped())
            .stderr(std::process::Stdio::null())
            .output()
            .await
            .with_context(|| format!("failed to run git {:?} in {}", args, repo.display()))?;
        if !output.status.success() {
            return Err(anyhow::anyhow!(
                "git {:?} failed in {}: exit {}",
                args,
                repo.display(),
                output.status
            ));
        }
        Ok(parse_name_status_z(&output.stdout))
    }
    
    /// Git status rank for sorting: higher = more relevant to sync.
    #[cfg(test)]
    pub(crate) fn fallback_status_rank(status: &FileStatus) -> u8 {
        match status {
            FileStatus::Deleted => 5,
            FileStatus::Renamed => 4,
            FileStatus::TypeChange => 3,
            FileStatus::Added => 2,
            FileStatus::Modified => 1,
            FileStatus::Unknown => 0,
            _ => 0,
        }
    }
    
    /// Attribute slow classification to its actual subprocess phase, including
    /// cancellation by the caller's timeout. This guard reports future lifetime;
    /// it does not claim that dropping the future terminated the subprocess.
    struct ClassificationPhase<'a> {
        repo: &'a Path,
        name: &'static str,
        started: std::time::Instant,
        outcome: &'static str,
    }
    
    impl<'a> ClassificationPhase<'a> {
        fn start(repo: &'a Path, name: &'static str) -> Self {
            Self {
                repo,
                name,
                started: std::time::Instant::now(),
                outcome: "interrupted",
            }
        }
    }
    
    impl Drop for ClassificationPhase<'_> {
        fn drop(&mut self) {
            let elapsed = self.started.elapsed();
            if crate::policy::debug_enabled() || elapsed >= std::time::Duration::from_secs(5) {
                eprintln!(
                    "classification: phase={} repo={} elapsed_ms={} outcome={}",
                    self.name,
                    self.repo.display(),
                    elapsed.as_millis(),
                    self.outcome,
                );
            }
        }
    }
    
    /// Get diff entries via `git diff` CLI (fallback when libgit2 fails).
    pub(crate) async fn cli_diff_entries(
        repo: &Path,
        budget: std::time::Duration,
    ) -> Result<Vec<DiffFile>> {
        let mut phase = ClassificationPhase::start(repo, "filter-aware-diff");
        // CHANGED 2026-07-21 (v0.112.33, audit M17/F2.8): `-z` + exit
        // status checked (was: status unchecked — a failed diff read as
        // "no changes"). CHANGED 2026-09-17: the child is spawned with its
        // own process group and kill_on_drop, so cancelling this future
        // (scheduler classification timeout) terminates git AND any spawned
        // warden filter children instead of leaking them to contend with
        // the retry. Regression:
        // classification_cancellation_terminates_git_process_group.
        let child = crate::git::spawn_git_command_cancellable(
            repo,
            &["diff", "--name-status", "-z", "HEAD"],
            "diff --name-status -z HEAD",
        )?;
        let (status, stdout, _stderr) = tokio::time::timeout(
            budget,
            crate::git::run_git_captured_output(child, repo, "diff --name-status -z HEAD"),
        )
        .await
        .with_context(|| {
            format!(
                "git diff --name-status -z HEAD timed out after {}s (filter-aware pass over a warden-filtered repo)",
                budget.as_secs()
            )
        })??;
        if !status.success() {
            phase.outcome = "nonzero-exit";
            return Err(anyhow::anyhow!(
                "git diff --name-status -z HEAD failed in {}: exit {}",
                repo.display(),
                status
            ));
        }
        phase.outcome = "success";
        let mut entries = Vec::new();
        for (path, status) in parse_name_status_z(&stdout) {
            entries.push(DiffFile::new(path, status));
        }
        Ok(entries)
    }
    
    /// Get untracked file entries via `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard`.
    pub(crate) async fn untracked_entries(repo: &Path) -> Result<Vec<DiffFile>> {
        let mut phase = ClassificationPhase::start(repo, "untracked-discovery");
        let child = crate::git::spawn_git_command_cancellable(
            repo,
            &["ls-files", "--others", "--exclude-standard", "-z"],
            "ls-files --others --exclude-standard",
        )?;
        let (status, stdout, _stderr) =
            crate::git::run_git_captured_output(child, repo, "ls-files --others").await?;
        if !status.success() {
            phase.outcome = "nonzero-exit";
            return Err(anyhow::anyhow!(
                "git ls-files --others --exclude-standard failed in {}: exit {}",
                repo.display(),
                status
            ));
        }
        phase.outcome = "success";
        let mut entries = Vec::new();
        for path in parse_z_paths(&stdout) {
            entries.push(DiffFile::new(path, FileStatus::Added));
        }
        Ok(entries)
    }

        #[cfg(target_os = "linux")]
        fn process_is_running(pid: i32) -> bool {
            match std::fs::read_to_string(format!("/proc/{pid}/stat")) {
                Ok(stat) => {
                    let (_, rest) = stat.rsplit_once(") ").expect("valid proc stat");
                    !matches!(rest.as_bytes().first(), Some(b'Z' | b'X'))
                }
                Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => false,
                Err(e) => panic!("cannot inspect fixture PID {pid}: {e}"),
            }
        }

    /// the per-repo `exclude_remotes` override with the
    /// `codeberg_public_only` policy gate. This is the SAME logic the
    /// daemon runs in `sync.rs` and `daemon.rs` at push time, so the
    /// `repos` table and the daemon's actual behavior stay in sync.
    ///
    /// Returns a `Vec<String>` of remote names to exclude. The order
    /// matches the order in `repo_override.exclude_remotes`, with any
    /// policy-driven `"codeberg"` appended at the end (preserving
    /// deterministic output for tests).
    ///
    /// ADDED 2026-07-17 (goal `codeberg-public-only`).
    ///
    /// ADDED 2026-07-29 (v0.113.16): the report-side mirror of the
    /// daemon's FULL push-time remote filter. `effective_excluded_remotes`
    /// applies only the per-repo `exclude_remotes` + the
    /// codeberg-public-only visibility gate; the daemon's
    /// `push_mirror_remotes` additionally applies the v0.112.28
    /// quota-posture rule (`codeberg_push_excluded` — codeberg skipped
    /// when the repo has no codeberg tracking ref AND effective
    /// auto-create is off). Returning both lists from one place so
    /// `push_to_remotes` / `excluded_remotes` can never drift apart.
    ///
    /// Returns `(push_to, excluded)`.
    pub(crate) fn report_effective_remotes(
        policy: &crate::policy::SyncPolicy,
        repo_override: &crate::policy::RepoPolicyOverride,
        repo_path: &std::path::Path,
        too_big_for_github: bool,
    ) -> (Vec<String>, Vec<String>) {
        let mut excluded = effective_excluded_remotes(policy, repo_override, repo_path);
        if crate::git::multi_remote::codeberg_push_excluded_for_repo(
            &policy.remotes,
            repo_override.auto_create_on_codeberg,
            crate::git::multi_remote::has_codeberg_tracking_ref(repo_path),
            repo_path,
            policy.sync_visibility_interval_hours,
        ) && !excluded.iter().any(|e| e == "codeberg")
        {
            excluded.push("codeberg".to_string());
        }
        // v0.113.18 (audit M2): mirror the daemon's over-2-GiB github skip
        // (sync.rs:1807-1811 — the daemon adds github to combined_exclude
        // when the pack exceeds github's 2 GiB limit). Without this the
        // REM cell shows 🐙 for a repo the daemon deliberately skips.
        if too_big_for_github && !excluded.iter().any(|e| e == "github") {
            excluded.push("github".to_string());
        }
        let filtered = crate::git::multi_remote::filter_remotes_by_exclude(&policy.remotes, &excluded);
        let push_to = filtered.iter().map(|r| r.name.clone()).collect();
        (push_to, excluded)
    }
    
    pub(crate) fn effective_excluded_remotes(
        policy: &crate::policy::SyncPolicy,
        repo_override: &crate::policy::RepoPolicyOverride,
        repo_path: &std::path::Path,
    ) -> Vec<String> {
        let mut combined: Vec<String> = repo_override.exclude_remotes.clone();
        let codeberg_public_only_effective = repo_override
            .codeberg_public_only
            .unwrap_or(policy.codeberg_public_only);
        if codeberg_public_only_effective {
            let cached_priv = crate::visibility::cached_repo_visibility(
                repo_path,
                policy.sync_visibility_interval_hours,
            );
            let skip_codeberg = match cached_priv {
                Some(true) => true,
                Some(false) => false,
                None => true, // safe default
            };
            if skip_codeberg && !combined.iter().any(|e| e == "codeberg") {
                combined.push("codeberg".to_string());
            }
        }
        combined
    }

    /// Print the `repos` column legend. Invoked by `dracon-sync repos --legend`
    /// (2026-07-08) AND by the default report footer (v0.113.12, goal-list
    /// 2026-07-29: the operator was confused by the v0.113.8 columns even WITH
    /// the `--legend` pointer line — an explanation you have to remember to ask
    /// for doesn't explain). Rewritten in v0.113.12 to match the columns that
    /// actually ship in the rich table (the old text referenced removed columns:
    /// MOD, PUSH-TO, "Daemon =").
    fn print_repos_legend() {
        // CHANGED 2026-08-10 (operator request): replace the heavy
        // full-width table with a short, aligned glossary. The full-width
        // rule still separates the legend visually from the repos table,
        // while each line maps directly to one or more real table columns.
        // Clamped to >= LEGEND_MIN_WIDTH and <= 1000; long lines wrap using
        // terminal display width so emoji do not break alignment.
        let width = (terminal_width().unwrap_or(LEGEND_MIN_WIDTH as u16))
            .max(LEGEND_MIN_WIDTH as u16)
            .min(1000) as usize;
        for line in legend_display_lines(width) {
            println!("{line}");
        }
        println!();
    }
    
    const LEGEND_LABEL_WIDTH: usize = 11;
    
    /// Format the short glossary for a terminal of `width` display columns.
    /// Kept separate from stdout emission so layout and Unicode-width tests
    /// can exercise the exact lines shown to operators.
    fn legend_display_lines(width: usize) -> Vec<String> {
        let mut lines = vec![format!(
            "── legend {}",
            "─".repeat(width.saturating_sub(10))
        )];
        let text_width = width.saturating_sub(LEGEND_LABEL_WIDTH + 2);
        let continuation_indent = " ".repeat(LEGEND_LABEL_WIDTH + 2);
        for (label, text) in repos_legend_rows() {
            if label.is_empty() {
                lines.push(String::new());
                continue;
            }
            for (index, text_line) in wrap_legend_text(text, text_width).lines().enumerate() {
                if index == 0 {
                    lines.push(format!(
                        "{label:<label_width$}  {text_line}",
                        label_width = LEGEND_LABEL_WIDTH
                    ));
                } else {
                    lines.push(format!("{continuation_indent}{text_line}"));
                }
            }
        }
        lines
    }
    
    /// Wrap legend prose at word boundaries using terminal display width.
    /// Legend entries contain emoji, so byte/character counts are not enough.
    fn wrap_legend_text(value: &str, max_width: usize) -> String {
        if max_width == 0 {
            return String::new();
        }
        let mut lines = Vec::new();
        let mut current = String::new();
        let mut current_width = 0;
        for word in value.split_whitespace() {
            let word_width = unicode_width::UnicodeWidthStr::width(word);
            if current_width > 0 && current_width + 1 + word_width > max_width {
                lines.push(std::mem::take(&mut current));
                current_width = 0;
            }
            if current_width > 0 {
                current.push(' ');
                current_width += 1;
            }
            current.push_str(word);
            current_width += word_width;
        }
        if !current.is_empty() {
            lines.push(current);
        }
        lines.join("\n")
    }
    
    /// Narrow terminals get NO legend rather than a brokenly-wrapped one
    /// (the compact table tier prints there); `--legend` remains the
    /// on-demand escape hatch.
    const LEGEND_MIN_WIDTH: usize = 120;
    
    /// The legend as data (tests assert coverage + display width).
    /// ADDED 2026-07-30 (v0.113.25): single source of legend content as
    /// (label, text) rows; a ("","") row is a group-separating blank.
    /// `repos_legend_lines` formats these for tests/back-compat;
    /// `print_repos_legend` renders them as a comfy-table (operator:
    /// "make the legend table-like").
    fn pack_evidence_hint(
        too_large: bool,
        deferred: bool,
        cached_at: Option<Option<u64>>,
        now: u64,
    ) -> String {
        let verdict = if too_large {
            "guard triggered"
        } else {
            "guard clear"
        };
        let source = match cached_at {
            Some(Some(at)) => format!("cached {}s ago", now.saturating_sub(at)),
            Some(None) => "cached, age unknown".to_string(),
            None if deferred => return "GitHub pack check unknown — use repos --deep".to_string(),
            None => "measured this report".to_string(),
        };
        format!("GitHub pack {verdict} ({source}); 2 GiB/push, not repo size")
    }
    
    fn repos_legend_rows() -> &'static [(&'static str, &'static str)] {
        &[
            ("STATUS", "Current convergence: ✅ clean/idle · 🟡 queued · 🔄 working · ⏳ retrying · 🚫 excluded/blocked · 🔴 stalled · ❔ unknown"),
            (
                "ACTIVITY",
                "Fresh scheduler evidence, not last commit age: queued = reserved/eligible (including unstarted inspections); working = started worker; retrying = owned cancellation or a live cooldown",
            ),
            // v0.113.87: `⏸️ frozen` replaces `🟡 waiting` on every PENDING
            // row while the daemon is frozen — the queue is not moving
            // because the dispatcher is switched off, not because a push is
            // slow. Documented here because the legend is the column key.
            (
                "",
                "⏸️ PAUSED = outstanding work while the daemon is frozen; unchanged idle rows stay clean (see the notice)",
            ),
            ("", ""),
            (
                "REPO",
                "🔒 private (last known) · public/unknown · > submodule · name⚡branch",
            ),
            (
                "CHANGES",
                "📝 modified · 📦 staged · 🆕 untracked · 🚫 excluded",
            ),
            ("A/B", "↑ ahead · ↓ behind · — synced"),
            ("EVIDENCE", "Stalled requires an exhausted current push budget or eligible continuous dirt with no worker/gate and no admission for 15m. Old/missing scheduler evidence is unknown, never proof of a stall. Working is ownership, not an operation heartbeat."),
            ("IDLE", "Unchanged idle repos are clean even with old commits/push records. Excluded bytes remain outside daemon coverage; clean is local/upstream convergence, not proof of all mirrors, bucket durability or absence of secrets."),
            ("", ""),
            (
                "PUSH",
                "Last daemon-recorded push result + observation age: ✅ OK · ❌ FAIL · — unknown. Historical OK never proves current changes published. REF AGE is upstream commit age, NOT push time. 🩹 current history issue · 🔑 token missing.",
            ),
            (
                "REM",
                "🐙 github · 🦊 gitlab · 🗻 codeberg (active only; excluded not shown)",
            ),
            ("", ""),
            ("1H/6H/24H", "commit pulse: last 1h / 6h / 24h"),
            (
                "GIT SIZE",
                "local Git objects/history, not worktree, clone download or bucket bytes · own+nested (children also have rows; do not sum twice) · +? unmeasured nested · 🟡 own ≥1 GiB · 🔴 GitHub 2 GiB/push guard",
            ),
            ("TOUCHED", "latest commit author (mailmap identity)"),
            ("", ""),
            (
                "hint",
                "`dracon-sync repos <name>` = detail · `repos --legend` = this key",
            ),
        ]
    }
    
    #[cfg(test)]
    fn repos_legend_lines() -> Vec<String> {
        legend_display_lines(LEGEND_MIN_WIDTH)
    }
    
    /// Print the legend under every repos table, width-gated (v0.113.12).
    fn print_repos_legend_footer() {
        let width = terminal_width().unwrap_or(120) as usize;
        if width < LEGEND_MIN_WIDTH {
            println!(
                "{}",
                colorize(
                    "GIT SIZE: local Git history, not bucket/push bytes; own+nested, +? unknown.",
                    Color::DarkGrey
                )
            );
            return;
        }
        for line in [
            "📝 modified · 📦 staged · 🆕 untracked · 🚫 excluded · A/B ↑ahead ↓behind · 1H/6H/24H commits",
            "PUSH = last result + age · GIT SIZE = local objects/history, own+nested (not bucket or push bytes)",
            "GitHub limit = 2 GiB per push, NOT total repo size · +? = nested size unmeasured; use --deep",
            "Detail: dracon-sync repos <name> · Full key: dracon-sync repos --legend",
        ] {
            println!("{}", colorize(line, Color::DarkGrey));
        }
        println!();
    }
    
    /// ADDED 2026-07-24 (v0.112.40): short-lived TTL on the mtime-keyed
    /// size+pack cache. Without a TTL, the cache invalidates on every
    /// gitdir mtime change — and the daemon updates gitdirs constantly
    /// (commits, fetches, pushes, repacks). Result: a `repos` run while
    /// the daemon is active triggers ~7 multi-GiB `du -sb` calls (200ms+
    /// each), producing the 4-12s worst case. A 30s TTL means back-to-back
    /// `repos` calls (the common operator pattern: "look, then re-look")
        /// ADDED 2026-08-09 (v0.113.49, pi-goal-list-loop-audit cascade
        /// finding): the PUSH legend used to list 5 markers (✅ OK, 🟣 push
        /// in flight, ❌ FAIL, 🩹 broken history, 🔑 forge token missing)
        /// while the code emits 8 distinct cell labels via `push_cell_label`
        /// — three of which (🛑 STUCK, 🩹 BROKEN, 🚫 BLOCKED) were
        /// undocumented, plus ✅ INTENT. Operators seeing `🛑 STUCK` in the
        /// PUSH column had no legend entry to look it up. This test pins
        /// the legend text as the source of truth for cell labels: if a new
        /// `push_cell_label` arm is added without updating the legend, the
        /// test trips. Markers (🩹 for missing objects, 🔑 for forge token
        /// missing) are also asserted since the legend documents them.
        #[test]
        fn test_repos_legend_covers_all_push_cell_labels() {
            // Collect every documented cell label.
            let cell_label_outputs: Vec<String> = [Some(true), Some(false), None]
                .into_iter()
                .map(|result| {
                    let mut row = RepoReportRow::for_tests("/fixture");
                    row.health.last_push =
                        result.map(|succeeded| crate::daemon::push_history::Observation {
                            version: 1,
                            repo: row.repo.clone(),
                            attempted_at: timestamp_secs(),
                            succeeded,
                        });
                    current_health::push(&row)
                        .0
                        .split_whitespace()
                        .take(2)
                        .collect::<Vec<_>>()
                        .join(" ")
                })
                .collect();
            // The legend should contain every cell label's text. We
            // concatenate the legend rows into a single haystack and search
            // for each needle (case-sensitive, since the labels are
            // deliberate).
            let haystack: String = repos_legend_rows().iter().map(|(_, text)| *text).collect();
            for label in &cell_label_outputs {
                assert!(
                    haystack.contains(label.as_str()),
                    "PUSH legend missing cell label {label:?} (full legend haystack: {haystack:?})"
                );
            }
            // Markers — the legend must document the 🩹 and 🔑 markers
            // (appended after the cell label by `push_cell_with_markers`).
            assert!(
                haystack.contains('🩹'),
                "PUSH legend missing the 🩹 marker glyph"
            );
            assert!(
                haystack.contains('🔑'),
                "PUSH legend missing the 🔑 marker glyph"
            );
            // Sanity: the haystack itself comes from the PUSH row (not
            // some other row), so we also check it contains `push_status`
            // vocabulary like `OK` (which appears in both the PUSH row's
            // legend entry and possibly elsewhere). This catches a
            // regression where someone moves the labels to a different
            // legend row by mistake.
            let push_row = repos_legend_rows()
                .iter()
                .find(|(label, _)| *label == "PUSH")
                .map(|(_, text)| *text)
                .expect("PUSH row must exist in legend");
            for label in &cell_label_outputs {
                assert!(
                    push_row.contains(label.as_str()),
                    "PUSH row of legend missing cell label {label:?}: {push_row:?}"
                );
            }
        }

    # AGENTS.md — browser-extensions-shared
    
    ## dracon-sync daemon: git-history rules for agent loops
    
    This repo is watched by the **dracon-sync daemon**, which auto-commits
    working-tree changes within ~3-10 seconds and pushes them to all
    remotes immediately after.
    
    **NEVER rewrite history in this repo.** Specifically, never:
    
    - `git commit --amend` — any commit may already be pushed
    - `git rebase`, or `git reset --hard` to an earlier commit
    - `git filter-branch` / `git filter-repo`
    - `git push --force` / `--force-with-lease`
    
    The daemon's auto-generated commit messages (e.g.
    `2 file(s) in extensions [...] DELTA:+7/-2`) are **expected and fine**.
    Do not "fix" them by rewriting: a rewritten commit races the
    already-pushed original and creates a divergent branch. Amending a
    merge commit drops its second parent, so an amend-every-iteration loop
    (like the virtual-pet loop observed 2026-07-25) re-creates the
    divergence every ~2 minutes — forever.
    
    ### What to do instead
    
    - **CHANGED 2026-09-26: do NOT `git commit` (or `git add`) yourself.**
      "First committer wins" racing was retired after 2026-09-25/26, when
      loop-vs-daemon add/commit races left 7 stale `index.lock` files
      across 6 repos, each wedging its repo until an operator removed the
      lock. Leave the tree dirty — the daemon commits within seconds. To
      checkpoint with your own message, write it into a note file
      (NOTE.md / progress.md); the daemon commits the content, which is
      the durable record.
    - **Daemon already committed your WIP?** Leave it. Put any description
      in a note file; the daemon commits it next cycle.
    - **Diverged (↑N ↓M)?** `git pull --no-rebase` (merge), never rebase
      or force-push. Identical trees are common (amend races) and merge
      cleanly.
    
    Reference: `dracon-utilities/docs/design/incident-amend-race-and-trust-2026-07-25.md`.
    
    ## Repository topology: single flat repo, no nested git repos
    
    This repo is a **single flat git repo** — no submodules, no nested
    standalone `.git` directories. All extensions and collections commit
    directly here. The last nested repo (`extensions/collections/new-tab/
    bookmarks-new-tab`) was flattened into regular tracked files on
    2026-08-05 (commit `6398285253`; full nested history preserved in
    `~/dracon/backups/bookmarks-new-tab-20260805.bundle` and the
    `DraconDev/bookmarks-new-tab` github/gitlab archives).
    
    If a loop ever initializes a nested git repo inside this worktree,
    remove its `.git` and track the files as plain content instead — never
    leave a gitlink or submodule arrangement. It also keeps the daemon's
    nested-repo auto-discovery from picking the nested repo up as a
    separate watched repo.
    
    ## Store listing copy: always ship a paste-ready .txt
    
    Chrome Web Store and AMO listing fields take plain text, not markdown. Any extension with a `STORE_LISTING.md` must also ship a paste-ready `STORE_LISTING.txt` beside it: no bold markers, no `#` headings, endashes converted to plain hyphens, short description within its character limit. `scripts/check-store-assets.py` warns (`?` lines, non-failing) when the `.txt` sibling is missing or still contains markdown markers. Precedent: `youtube-dislike/STORE_LISTING.txt` (2026-09-08), `death-note-typing-practice/CHROME_WEB_STORE_COPY_PASTE.txt`.
    
    ## Virtual-pet agent loop (intentional, scoped)
    
    **Date**: 2026-07-28 (goal `20260728012220-o3273t`).
    
    The `extensions/collections/new-tab/virtual-pet-new-tab/` extension is iterated by
    a long-running agent loop (glla workdir binding). The loop is
    intentional; its trust scope is:
    
    - **Path-scoped to** `extensions/collections/new-tab/virtual-pet-new-tab/` only.
      Note: a standalone twin, `extensions/standalones/virtual-pet/`, now also
      exists in this repo (added later by fleet-wide passes — it shares the
      `lib/review-ask.ts` / warden release infrastructure but is a separate
      product). The twin is NOT part of the loop's path scope; changes to it
      come from fleet goals and manual commits, exactly like any other
      standalone.
    - **Does NOT touch** `affiliate/`, `collections/`,
      `extensions/standalones/auto-form-filler/`, root-level files,
      or any other workspace member. Cross-workspace commits observed
      in this repo are manual `DraconDev` commits, not loop output.
    - **Loop self-quiesces** when no goal is active (state
      `goal: false, list: 0, loop: false` in
      `.pi-glla/active.jsonl`). Resume by `propose_goal_draft`
      against the workdir; the loop wakes on demand.
    
    The no-history-rewrite rule above applies; the loop must NEVER
    `commit --amend` / `rebase` / `filter-repo` / `--force-with-lease`.

        /// Verify the sum of all 16 column minimums in `print_repos_compact_table`
        /// plus 15 borders stays within the advisory 244-col floor (REFRESHED
        /// 2026-10-03, audit R3-L38: was "< 220 cols (Vertical is for < 220)"
        /// — Compact is auto-picked for < 165 since v0.113.26, so the 242
        /// floor exceeds narrow terminals and comfy-table squashes).
        ///
        /// 2026-07-19 (goal `4555eaf6`): REPO (18), ROLE (14), PUBLISH (18),
        /// PUSH-TO (32), LAST COMMIT (18), STATE+ACT (17), HINT (26) all
        /// became Absolute so cells with variable-length content
        /// (`pully-fully-pull-based-fleet-reconciler`, `released/one-mil-girls`,
        /// `⚠️ origin/main (gone)`, etc.) are truncated rather than letter-wrapped
        /// onto a second line on narrow terminals.
        #[test]
        fn test_branch_cell_content_truncates_to_nine() {
            // ADDED 2026-10-03 (audit L17): shared compact/full BRANCH
            // shaper (Absolute(11) − padding). Grapheme-safe: no half-flag.
            assert_eq!(branch_cell_content("main"), "main");
            let flag = "\u{1f1eb}\u{1f1f7}";
            let cell = branch_cell_content(&format!("ab{flag}cdefghij"));
            let w: usize = cell
                .chars()
                .map(|c| unicode_width::UnicodeWidthChar::width(c).unwrap_or(0))
                .sum();
            assert!(w <= 9, "branch cell must fit 9 cols: {cell:?} ({w})");
            assert!(cell.ends_with('…'), "long branch truncates: {cell:?}");
            assert!(
                cell.contains(flag),
                "grapheme kept whole, not split: {cell:?}"
            );
        }
    
        #[test]
        fn test_compact_table_min_width_within_250() {
            // The values here MUST match the set_constraints in print_repos_compact_table.
            // If you change the table layout, update both at once.
            // 16 cols: #, STATUS, REPO, ROLE, BRANCH, PUBLISH, MOD, STG, UT,
            // AHEAD, BEHIND, PUSH, PUSH-TO, LAST COMMIT, STATE+ACT, HINT.
            // R3-L38 (2026-10-03): HINT 22 → 26 — the array never caught
            // the 2026-07-19 bump production carries (its own MUST-match
            // contract was violated).
            let minimums: [u16; 16] = [4, 13, 18, 14, 11, 18, 8, 8, 7, 9, 11, 13, 32, 18, 17, 26];
            let sum: u32 = minimums.iter().map(|&x| x as u32).sum();
            let borders: u32 = 15;
            let total = sum + borders;
            // 2026-07-19 (goal `4555eaf6` v0.112.25): threshold bumped
            // 240 → 244 to match the new HINT column bump (22 → 26).
            // The 227 cols minimum + 15 borders + 2 headroom is
            // unavoidable because PUSH-TO 32, HINT 26, REPO 18, ROLE 14,
            // PUBLISH 18 are all needed to fit variable-length content
            // on narrow terminals.
            assert_eq!(
                total, 242,
                "Compact table floor moved from the advisory 242 cols: update \
                 the array above and the constraints together."
            );
        }

            assert!(

                "test setup: long_msg should be >100 chars, got {}",
                long_msg.chars().count()

            let raw = format!("abcdef1 {}", long_msg);
    
            let width = |s: &str| -> usize {

    /**
     * No dead exports.
     *
     * An exported symbol in a browser extension has no external consumer:
     * the extension IS the app. So an export nothing imports is not a
     * public API — it is a leftover that reads like one, and it rots.
     * The Pass 11 scout found nine of them (syncUsagePercent, the
     * isSiteBlocked re-export, EMPTY_BLOCKLIST, COLLECTION_KEYS, the
     * catch-commit re-exports, lib/game/clock.ts, TYPE_HEX, qualityLabel,
     * SpeciesThumb's showBadge prop, CueController.unmount); they were
     * removed, and this check is what stops the next one from appearing.
     *
     * How it works: every exported name in lib/ and entrypoints/ must
     * appear somewhere else in the repository. The check is deliberately
     * conservative — it counts name occurrences across every source file,
     * so a name that collides with another module's symbol can hide a
     * dead export (a false negative) but can never wrongly flag a live
     * one. A guard that cries wolf gets switched off; this one stays.
     */
    import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
    import { readdirSync, readFileSync, statSync } from 'node:fs';
    import { join } from 'node:path';
    
    // The project root: vitest runs with the package directory as its cwd.
    // (import.meta.url is rewritten by the Vite pipeline here, so it is not
    // a usable path source.)
    const ROOT = process.cwd();
    
    /** Directories whose sources ship inside the extension. */
    const SOURCE_DIRS = ['lib', 'entrypoints'];
    const SOURCE_EXT = /\.(ts|svelte)$/;
    const CORPUS_EXT = /\.(ts|svelte|mjs|js|json)$/;
    const SKIP_DIRS = new Set(['node_modules', '.output', '.wxt', 'coverage', 'dist', '.git']);
    
    function walk(dir: string, out: string[] = []): string[] {
      let entries: string[];
      try {
        entries = readdirSync(dir);
      } catch {
        return out;
      }
      for (const name of entries) {
        if (SKIP_DIRS.has(name)) continue;
        const full = join(dir, name);
        if (statSync(full).isDirectory()) walk(full, out);
        else out.push(full);
      }
      return out;
    }
    
    const ALL_FILES = [
      ...walk(join(ROOT, 'lib')),
      ...walk(join(ROOT, 'entrypoints')),
      ...walk(join(ROOT, 'tests')),
      ...walk(join(ROOT, 'scripts')),
      ...walk(join(ROOT, 'tools')),
      ...walk(join(ROOT, 'store-assets')),
      ...readdirSync(ROOT)
        .filter((f) => CORPUS_EXT.test(f) && statSync(join(ROOT, f)).isFile())
        .map((f) => join(ROOT, f)),
    ];
    
    /**
     * This file names the symbols it guards against (in its own comments),
     * so it can never count as a USAGE of them: a dead export that this
     * file mentions by name would otherwise look alive. The corpus and the
     * per-file scans therefore skip it.
     */
    const SELF = 'dead-exports.test.ts';
    const OTHER_FILES = ALL_FILES.filter((f) => !f.endsWith(SELF));
    const CORPUS_WITHOUT_SELF = OTHER_FILES.map((f) => readFileSync(f, 'utf8')).join('\n');
    
    const DECLARATION = /export\s+(?:async\s+)?(?:const|function|class|let|var|interface|type|enum)\s+([A-Za-z0-9_$]+)/g;
    const RE_EXPORT_LIST = /export\s*\{([^}]*)\}/g;
    
    interface Exported {
      name: string;
      file: string;
    }
    
    function collectExports(): Exported[] {
      const found: Exported[] = [];
      for (const dir of SOURCE_DIRS) {
        for (const file of walk(join(ROOT, dir))) {
          if (!SOURCE_EXT.test(file)) continue;
          const src = readFileSync(file, 'utf8');
          for (const match of src.matchAll(DECLARATION)) {
            found.push({ name: match[1], file: file.slice(ROOT.length) });
          }
          for (const match of src.matchAll(RE_EXPORT_LIST)) {
            for (const part of match[1].split(',')) {
              const name = part.trim().split(/\s+as\s+/).pop()?.trim();
              if (name) found.push({ name, file: file.slice(ROOT.length) });
            }
          }
        }
      }
      return found;
    }
    
    describe('dead exports', () => {
      it('finds no exported symbol that nothing imports', () => {
        expect(
          readdirSync(ROOT).includes('package.json'),
          'the scan must run from the project root',
        ).toBe(true);
        const exported = collectExports();
        expect(exported.length, 'the scan found no exports at all — the scanner is broken')
          .toBeGreaterThan(50);
    
        const dead: string[] = [];
        for (const { name, file } of exported) {
          const uses =
            CORPUS_WITHOUT_SELF.match(new RegExp(`\\b${name.replace(/\$/g, '\\$')}\\b`, 'g')) ?? [];
          // One occurrence is the declaration itself; anything beyond that
          // is a real reference somewhere in the repository.
          if (uses.length <= 1) dead.push(`${name} (${file})`);
        }
    
        expect(
          dead,
          'these exports are referenced nowhere in the repository. A browser extension has no external consumers, so an export nothing imports is a leftover that reads like a public API — remove it, or wire it up.',
        ).toEqual([]);
      });
    
      it('finds no component prop that no caller ever passes', () => {
        // A prop is a component's public API in the same way an export is.
        // SpeciesThumb's `showBadge` sat in the Props interface and in the
        // $props() destructure and was rendered in the template — and no
        // caller ever set it, so the badge could never appear. The prop
        // looked live and shipped as dead surface.
        const sources = ALL_FILES.filter((f) => f.endsWith('.svelte'));
        const dead: string[] = [];
        for (const file of sources) {
          const src = readFileSync(file, 'utf8');
          const destructure = src.match(/let\s*\{([^}]*)\}\s*(?::[^=]*)?=\s*\$props\(\)/s);
          if (!destructure) continue;
          const props = destructure[1]
            .split(',')
            .map((part) => part.split(':')[0].split('=')[0].trim())
            .filter(Boolean);
          for (const prop of props) {
            const passed = OTHER_FILES.some(
              (other) =>
                other !== file &&
                new RegExp(`\\b${prop.replace(/\$/g, '\\$')}\\b`).test(readFileSync(other, 'utf8')),
            );
            if (!passed) dead.push(`${prop} (${file.slice(ROOT.length)})`);
          }
        }
    
        expect(
          dead,
          'these props are never passed by any caller, so they are dead surface: remove them, or let a caller use them.',
        ).toEqual([]);
      });
    });

    /** Mean volume in dBFS, measured with ffmpeg's volumedetect. */
    async function meanVolumeDb(file: string): Promise<number> {
      return measureDb(file, 'mean_volume');
    }
    
    /** Peak volume in dBFS, measured with ffmpeg's volumedetect. */
    async function peakVolumeDb(file: string): Promise<number> {
      return measureDb(file, 'max_volume');
    }
    
    /** Decode a file to mono float samples, for the loop-seam check. */
    async function decodePcm(file: string): Promise<number[]> {
      const { execFile } = await import('node:child_process');
      const { promisify } = await import('node:util');
      const run = promisify(execFile);
      // `encoding: 'buffer'` matters: execFile hands back a utf8 STRING
      // by default, and Buffer.from(string) re-encodes those bytes as
      // text — which turns the audio into noise. The seam check was
      // measuring that noise.
      const { stdout } = await run('ffmpeg', [
        '-hide_banner',
        '-i', file,
        '-f', 's16le',
        '-ac', '1',
        '-ar', '22050',
        '-',
      ], { maxBuffer: 64 * 1024 * 1024, encoding: 'buffer' });
      const raw = Buffer.isBuffer(stdout) ? stdout : Buffer.from(stdout as unknown as string, 'binary');
      const samples: number[] = [];
      for (let i = 0; i + 1 < raw.length; i += 2) {
        samples.push(raw.readInt16LE(i) / 32768);
      }
      return samples;
    }
    
    async function measureDb(file: string, field: 'mean_volume' | 'max_volume'): Promise<number> {
      const { execFile } = await import('node:child_process');
      const { promisify } = await import('node:util');
      const run = promisify(execFile);
      // volumedetect writes to stderr.
      const { stderr } = await run('ffmpeg', ['-hide_banner', '-i', file, '-af', 'volumedetect', '-f', 'null', '-'])
        .catch((err: { stderr?: string }) => ({ stderr: err.stderr ?? '' }));
      const match = stderr.match(new RegExp(`${field}:\\s*(-?[\\d.]+) dB`));
      if (!match) throw new Error(`ffmpeg reported no ${field} for ${file}`);
      return Number(match[1]);
    }
    
    /**
     * The mix spec, mirrored from tools/package-sfx.py: every moment has a

     */
        const run = promisify(execFile);
        ffmpegAvailable = await run('ffmpeg', ['-version'])
          .then(() => true)

      }

    /** Check a directory of packaged samples against the mix spec.
     *
     * The measurements run concurrently: each one spawns an ffmpeg
     * process, and doing thirteen of them one after another made this
     * check slow enough to time out when the suite ran in parallel.
     */
    async function evaluateMix(dir: string): Promise<MixViolation[]> {
      const checks = await Promise.all(
        SFX_MOMENTS.map(async (moment): Promise<MixViolation | null> => {
          const file = path.join(dir, `${moment}.mp3`);
          if (!existsSync(file)) {
            return { moment, reason: `${moment}.mp3 missing` };
          }
          const [low, high] = MIX_BANDS[moment];
          const [mean, peak] = await Promise.all([meanVolumeDb(file), peakVolumeDb(file)]);
          const violations: MixViolation[] = [];
          if (mean < low || mean > high) {
            violations.push({ moment, reason: `${moment} mean ${mean} dBFS outside ${low}..${high}` });
          }
          if (peak > PEAK_CEILING_DB) {
            violations.push({ moment, reason: `${moment} peak ${peak} dBFS above ${PEAK_CEILING_DB}` });
          }
          return violations.length ? violations[0] : null;
        }),
      );
      return checks.filter((v): v is MixViolation => v !== null);
    }

    <script lang="ts">
      /**
       * Theme player — mounts the collection theme for a surface.
       *
       * The theme engine is a page-wide singleton, so a surface that
       * wants music asks for it (lib/game/theme-holders) rather than
       * driving the engine itself. This component is the whole job:
       * read the record, prime the audio engine from it, and hold the
       * theme for as long as it is mounted.
       *
       * Two props, because two surfaces want it for different reasons:
       *
       *  - `holder` names the vote, so the Dex and the settings shell can
       *    both want the theme without either stopping the other's.
       *  - `enabled` says whether this surface wants it at all. The
       *    settings shell passes the player's "music in settings" switch,
       *    so the music there is a choice rather than a surprise.
       */
      import { onMount } from 'svelte';
      import { setThemeVisible, unlockAudio } from '@/lib/game/music';
      import { primeAudioFromRecord } from '@/lib/game/audio-priming';
      import { releaseTheme, wantTheme } from '@/lib/game/theme-holders';
    
      interface Props {
        /** Which vote this surface holds. */
        holder: 'dex' | 'settings';
        /** Whether this surface wants the theme right now. */
        enabled?: boolean;
      }
      const { holder, enabled = true }: Props = $props();
    
      /**
       * Whether the vote has been taken yet. The theme must not start
       * before the record has been read: the engine's mute mirror starts
       * at "sound on", so a theme that began early would be audible for a
       * player who had turned the sound off. The flag keeps the switch
       * below from taking the vote before the priming is done.
       */
      let primed = $state(false);
    
      onMount(() => {
        let cancelled = false;
        void (async () => {
          await primeAudioFromRecord();
          if (cancelled) return;
          primed = true;
          if (enabled) wantTheme(holder);
        })();
    
        const onVisibility = () => setThemeVisible(document.visibilityState === 'visible');
        document.addEventListener('visibilitychange', onVisibility);
    
        // The first gesture anywhere on the page unlocks the audio: a
        // browser refuses to make noise before the user has interacted,
        // and the theme waits for that. It listens on the document rather
        // than on the section, so no visible element has to pretend to be
        // a button.
        const onGesture = () => unlockAudio();
        document.addEventListener('pointerdown', onGesture);
        document.addEventListener('keydown', onGesture);
    
        return () => {
          cancelled = true;
          document.removeEventListener('visibilitychange', onVisibility);
          document.removeEventListener('pointerdown', onGesture);
          document.removeEventListener('keydown', onGesture);
          releaseTheme(holder);
        };
      });
    
      // When the surface's own switch flips, the theme follows: the
      // holder takes the vote back or gives it up. Before the record has
      // been read the vote is not taken at all — the switch is applied
      // once, when the priming lands.
      $effect(() => {
        if (!primed) return;
        if (enabled) wantTheme(holder);
        else releaseTheme(holder);
      });
    </script>

    /**
     * Who owns the collection theme.
     *
     * The theme engine (lib/game/music.ts) is a module singleton: one
     * AudioContext, one looping source, for the whole page. That is right
     * — two contexts playing the same track is a bug, not a feature — but
     * it means the surfaces that want music cannot each call
     * `startTheme()`/`stopTheme()` for themselves. The Dex wants the
     * theme; the settings shell may want it too (the player can turn
     * that on). If both drove the engine directly, leaving the Dex would
     * stop the music for the settings page.
     *
     * So the surfaces report what they want, and this module keeps the
     * count: the theme plays while at least one surface wants it, and
     * stops when the last one lets go. The engine sees one start and one
     * stop, whoever asked.
     */
    import { startTheme, stopTheme } from './music';
    
    /** The surfaces that can want the theme. Each holds one vote. */
    type Holder = 'dex' | 'settings';
    
    const holders = new Set<Holder>();
    
    /**
     * A surface wants the theme. Calling it twice for the same holder is
     * one vote, not two — a re-render must not double the count.
     */
    export function wantTheme(holder: Holder): void {
      if (holders.has(holder)) return;
      holders.add(holder);
      if (holders.size === 1) startTheme();
    }
    
    /**
     * A surface no longer wants the theme. The music stops only when the
     * last holder lets go.
     */
    export function releaseTheme(holder: Holder): void {
      if (!holders.has(holder)) return;
      holders.delete(holder);
      if (holders.size === 0) stopTheme();
    }
    
    /** True while some surface wants the theme. */
    export function themeWanted(): boolean {
      return holders.size > 0;
    }
    
    /** Forgets every holder. A test that has already asked for the theme
     *  would otherwise leave the music wanted for the tests after it. */
    export function resetThemeHolders(): void {
      holders.clear();
    }
    /**
     * Priming the audio engines from the synced record.
     *
     * The sound engine keeps the player's mute and volume in an in-memory
     * mirror so playback never awaits storage — and that mirror starts at
     * "sound on". Every surface that can make a sound therefore has to
     * fill it from the record before it plays, or it plays for a player
     * who turned the sound off.
     *
     * The Dex was the one surface that did not, and the collection theme
     * played at full volume for a player who had muted the game. This
     * module is the single place that reads the record and pushes it into
     * both engines, so a surface cannot apply half of it (the music
     * fields without the effects ones) by accident.
     */
    import { loadSettings, type TabmonSettings } from '../settings';
    import { applyAudioSettings } from './sound';
    import { applyMusicSettings } from './music';
    
    /**
     * Fills the audio engines from the synced record.
     *
     * Returns the record it read, or null when the read failed — in which
     * case the engines keep their defaults (sound on), which is what
     * every surface did before.
     */
    export async function primeAudioFromRecord(): Promise<TabmonSettings | null> {
      const settings = await loadSettings().catch(() => null);
      if (!settings) return null;
      // The master switch is global: it silences the effects AND the
      // theme, so the effects fields go in first.
      applyAudioSettings({
        muted: settings.soundMuted,
        volume: settings.soundVolume,
      });
      applyMusicSettings({
        muted: settings.soundMusicMuted ?? false,
        volume: settings.soundMusicVolume ?? 0.4,
        theme: settings.soundTheme,
      });
      return settings;
    }

     * first click (browsers block audio before a gesture), it stops when
